subject: ITAL
course_description: Topics to be announced each semester. Course content will vary, including topics of literature, history, culture, art history, political thought, business, current trends, and more. May be repeated for credit when syllabus changes.
course_notes: ITAL 276. Italian Cinema: Neorealism to the Present (same as FILM 286) Prof. Achille Castaldo Tuesdays/Thursdays 11:30am-12:45pm. Content: A history of Italian cinema from the mid-20th century to the present, with a focus on neorealist films and aesthetics in light of their international resonance. This class will address both major and lesser-known movements, directors, and genres, devoting particular attention to historical topics including fascism and antifascism, youth culture, class struggle, terrorism, mafia, and migration. Film aesthetics topics will include the construction of pathos, landscape, memory, and charisma. Authors will include well-known personalities such as Roberto Rossellini, Michelangelo Antonioni, Pierpaolo Pasolini, Lina Wertmüller, Liliana Cavani, and contemporary filmmakers who are renewing Italian cinema, such as Alice Rohrwacher and Laura Bispuri. Class will be in English. Weekly online screening required (all films will be subtitled in English).
